title: Trespassers in Our Own Homes
logline: A corporate town's operating charter is unexpectedly revoked, turning every resident into a trespasser overnight.

roles.description: Elected to manage potholes, now trying to lead a guerrilla defense.
An aging veteran teaching miners how to fire anti-ship weaponry.
A massive, automated repossession vessel equipped with riot suppression gear.
A sprawling subterranean settlement built entirely out of retrofitted shipping crates.
A distant neutral jurisdiction where a single honest judge holds court.
A distant board of directors deciding the fate of thousands via spreadsheet.
Desperate locals armed with mining lasers and hunting rifles.

public_situation: The {role:corporate_conglomerate} has officially revoked the charter for a local settlement, giving the residents 24 hours to vacate their homes.
private_truth: The corporation discovered a massive vein of thorium directly beneath the town and manufactured a charter violation to steal the land.

beats.public_change: The corporate conglomerate cuts off all external power and life support to the town.

missions.reason: Needs raw thorium delivered so the militia can jury-rig an explosive perimeter around the primary airlocks.
missions.private_fact: The defender knows explosives won't stop ship weapons, but needs the townspeople to feel like they are doing something.

missions.reason: Hires the pilot to officially dock at the distant court and submit the town's original physical founding charter to a sympathetic judge.
missions.private_fact: The mayor is spending the town's entire emergency fund on this single courier run.

beats.public_change: The massive corporate evictor ship enters orbit and begins broadcasting dispersal warnings.

missions.reason: Hires the pilot to intercept and destroy the evictor ship before it can breach the town's hull.
missions.private_fact: The corporate ship offers to pay the pilot double to simply leave the sector and let the eviction proceed.

beats.public_change: The destruction of the evictor pauses the assault, but corporate lawyers demand a final arbitration.

missions.reason: Needs the pilot to scan the old boundary beacons near the town's perimeter to mathematically prove it was established before the corporation claimed the sector.
missions.private_fact: The scans show the beacons were moved ten meters three years ago, technically invalidating the town's claim.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot falsifies the beacon scan to support the town.
resolutions.summary: The town's charter is upheld. The corporation backs down, and the militia becomes a permanent, hardened defense force.

consequences.public_summary: A pilot helped a small town legally tell a massive corporation to go straight to hell.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot reports the true beacon locations.
resolutions.summary: The corporation legally annexes the town. The militia is arrested, the residents are evicted, and the mayor is fired.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot takes the corporate offer and abandons the town.
resolutions.summary: Without defense, the town is violently breached. Many die, the rest flee, and the corporation strip-mines the ruins.

loose_threads.detail: The tractor beam signatures used to quietly move the beacons perfectly match the town's own aging defense grid.
The destroyed corporate evictor ship's core programming contained a subroutine specifically designed to target the town's water filtration systems first.

radio_hooks: Unconfirmed reports of armed resistance from {role:town_militia}.

voice_direction.town_mayor: Loud, practiced public speaking rhythm, even in private. Avoids admitting fear.
voice_direction.town_defender: Gruff, practical tone. Focuses purely on logistics and angles of fire.
